title: Revert a Bad Release through a New Reviewed Deployment
objectives: Revert a Bad Release through a New Reviewed Deployment
Verify state independently and preserve the source/deployment boundary.

tasks.instruction: Use the isolated Lab attempt. Open Terminal: ssh svc_ansible@ansible01 then cd ~/splunk-automation. V7 source additions are precommitted for this lesson; free practice can add them in Automation Operations. Commands and services are simulated.

The fixture deployed a template change with sourcetype v7_broken. Inspect git log and identify that source commit. Set a training Git identity if needed (git config user.name Learner and git config user.email learner@example.test). Create a recovery branch, git revert that non-merge commit, and push. Review/check/approve/merge the recovery PR, then run committed main playbooks/v7_inputs.yml on ds01. The effective sourcetype must return to v7_automation; rewriting branch history or changing target files alone is insufficient.
Use the run output and independent configuration inspection to answer the evidence question. The source and operational checks must also pass.

hints: Inspect source, target scope and the latest run before retrying.
Use --limit ds01 and inspect btool after an actual apply.

references.purpose: Handlers run on change in definition order

checks.label: Revert is preserved in reviewed main history and deployed
Running input matches the requested sourcetype

questions.prompt: Which sourcetype was restored by the reviewed revert deployment?

setup.text:
[monitor://{{ practice_source }}]
index = {{ practice_index }}
sourcetype = v7_broken
disabled = false

feedback.success: Verified actual source, scoped execution and target state.
feedback.incomplete: Check the latest scoped run, source revision, ownership and activation. An answer or command text alone is insufficient.
